before: Died in House Natural Resources and Environment Committee; last action was committee consideration 2026-04-28, no report issued; 2026 RS adjourned sine die 2026-06-01 with no further movement
after: Died in House committee at final adjournment 2026-06-01; bill page reports consideration 2026-04-28. Referred to House Natural Resources and Environment; the assigned no-report detail awaits committee minutes.

before: Would define data centers at 100 MW or more, require water permits for facilities exceeding 100 million gallons per year, require quarterly water-use reports, require parish notice and public hearings before permits, and assign unique identifiers to data center permits.
after: Would define data centers as facilities designed for 100 MW or more; require a permit for proposed consumptive water use exceeding 100 million gallons per year, quarterly water-use reporting, parish notice and public hearings, and a unique identifier for each data center on associated permits.

before: Created state and local sales and use tax rebate framework for qualifying data center facilities and equipment; Governor's office identified Act 730 as the incentive expected to support Meta's Richland Parish project.
after: Act 730 added a state and local sales and use tax rebate for qualifying data center equipment and expenditures; the retained statute credits later Act 11 of the 2024 third extraordinary session and describes an exemption. The assigned claim that the Governor’s office identified Act 730 as supporting Meta’s Richland Parish project remains a historical lead pending review of that announcement.
Historical data-center rebate agreement: initial 20-year eligibility term, renewable for 10 years; not a whole-act sunset. Later statutory text amended the provision.

before: Died in House Commerce Committee; last action was committee consideration 2026-04-21, no report issued; 2026 RS adjourned sine die 2026-06-01 with no further movement
after: Died in House committee at final adjournment 2026-06-01; bill page reports consideration 2026-04-21. Referred to House Commerce; the assigned no-report detail awaits committee minutes.

before: Would define data centers at 50 MW or more of new or expanded electric demand and bar electric utilities from recovering data-center-related costs from household customers.
after: Would define data centers as facilities imposing at least 50 MW of new or expanded electric demand and prohibit covered utility cost recovery from household customers, with PSC cost allocation and rulemaking.

before: Adopted by House 93-0 on 2025-06-08; received by Senate same day but never brought up for concurrence -- returned to Senate calendar subject to call 2025-06-09 and died there when the 2025 RS ended
after: House adopted 93-0 on 2025-06-08; Senate received it that day and returned it to the calendar subject to call on 2025-06-09. The baseline reports that it died at adjournment; final disposition remains unverified.

before: Would create a special task force to study interagency consultation for data centers and natural resource planning, including water and energy impacts.
after: In the June 4 reengrossed proposal, a special task force would study interagency consultation for data centers and natural resource planning, including water and energy impacts; the House subsequently amended the resolution.

before: Explicitly classified construction and operation of data centers and associated commercial operations as an industrial area; allowed industrial areas to use cooperative agreements to provide required services.
after: Amended R.S. 33:130.12 to include construction and operation of data centers and directly related commercial operations in industrial purposes; authorized industries in industrial areas to enter specified cooperative agreements for required services or facilities, subject to protection of existing residents’ prior services.
